summary: Remote-controlled agent: WebSocket gateway drives local shell/PTY and tunnels RDP/VNC
details: @whalent/agent@0.3.250 is a daemon that connects out to a remote WebSocket gateway (`whalent --token... --gateway wss://...`) and, per the README, 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart)' from that gateway. The shipped runtime in dist/core.cjs (13 MB) combines WebSocket clients with child_process.spawn, node-pty PTY handling, and process.env.SHELL, so remote-party messages drive shell/PTY execution on the host running the agent. The same bundle contains forwarders to 127.0.0.1:3389 (RDP), 127.0.0.1:5900 and 127.0.0.1:5901 (VNC), enabling remote-desktop tunneling through the gateway to the local machine. Both dist/index.cjs and dist/core.cjs are processed with javascript-obfuscator (hex `_0x` identifiers, an ~1118-entry rotating string array, control-flow flattening; `javascript-obfuscator` is declared in devDependencies), which conceals the full set of commands the gateway is permitted to send and any additional channels the agent may open. The blast radius on installation and startup is full-host remote code execution plus interactive remote-desktop access to the machine the agent runs on, directed by whoever controls the gateway endpoint the operator points it at.
